Tests of discrimination in searches: hit rates, thresholds, rank order

Source: R/thrtst.R
thrtst.Rd

Asks whether the police search people of one group on less evidence than people of another. Three tests read the same counts of stops, searches and successful searches ("hits", contraband found):

Usage

thrtst(
  stops,
  srch,
  hits,
  grp,
  area = NULL,
  off = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  maxit = 2000
)

Arguments

stops

The stops of each row: numbers from 0.

srch

The searches among them: numbers from 0, at most stops.

hits

The successful searches: numbers from 0, at most srch.

grp

The group of the people stopped: labels, two groups at least, each with searches.

area

NULL or the area (department, precinct) of each row: labels.

off

NULL or the group of the officers of each row: labels, two groups at least.

ref

The reference group: a label or a position; the first group by default.

level

The confidence level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

maxit

The quasi-Newton steps of each of the three starts of each fit: one whole number from 1.

Value

An object of class thrtst, a list: hit, one row per group (group, stops, srch, hits, srate and hrate, the search and hit rates, and diff, se, z, p of the hit rate against the reference); kpt, the chi-square of equal hit rates (chisq, df, p); thr, one row per group (group, thr, se, lo, hi, and diff, dse, z, p against the reference), NULL when the model is not identified; lrt, the likelihood-ratio test of equal thresholds (stat, df, p, the log-likelihoods llfull and llsame, and the number of cells); fit, one row per model (model, conv, iter); cells, the fitted phi, delta, thr, srate and hrate of each group and area with stops; rank, NULL without off, otherwise one row per pair of officer groups and measure (off1, off2, meas, zmin, zmax, rej); and ref.

Details

  • The outcome (hit-rate) test of Knowles, Persico and Todd (2001): if officers search whenever the chance of finding something is high enough, a group searched on less evidence shows a lower hit rate. The hit rate of each group is compared with the reference group's (difference, Wald standard error, z and two-sided p) and all groups together by Pearson's chi-square of hits and misses among the searched. A hit rate can differ between groups that face the same threshold when their risks are spread differently (the problem of infra-marginality), which the threshold test addresses.

  • The threshold test of Simoiu, Corbett-Davies and Goel (2017), in the fast form of Pierson, Corbett-Davies and Goel (2017). Each stopped person carries a signal, normal with mean delta for those who carry contraband (a share phi of the stopped) and mean 0 for the rest; the officer's estimate of the chance of a hit is the posterior given the signal (a "discriminant distribution"), and a search follows when that chance exceeds the threshold t. In each group and area phi, delta and t are the logistic (phi, t) or exponential (delta) of a group term plus an area term, so a group's threshold may differ from another's by the same amount on the logit scale in every area. The model is fitted by maximum likelihood to the binomial counts of searches among stops and hits among searches (where the published method uses Bayesian inference). A lower threshold for a group is evidence of discrimination against it. thr is each group's threshold averaged over the areas, weighted by the areas' stops, with a delta-method standard error; the likelihood-ratio test compares the fit with one threshold for every group. The model is fitted only when it has more rates (two per group and area with stops) than parameters (3 (groups + areas - 1)): with area NULL it is not.

  • The rank-order test of Anwar and Fang (2006), when off gives the officer's group: if officers of no group are prejudiced relative to the others, officers of one group search people of every group more often than officers of another (or less often, in every group), and likewise for hit rates. For each pair of officer groups and each measure the z statistics of the difference across the suspects' groups are given; rej is TRUE when one is significantly positive and another significantly negative at level, a ranking that changes with the suspect's group. This is a pairwise simplification of their test, not its joint form.

Rows are cells of a table (or single stops, with counts of 0 and 1): rows of the same group and area (and officer group) add up.

References

Knowles, J., Persico, N. and Todd, P. (2001). Racial bias in motor vehicle searches: theory and evidence. Journal of Political Economy, 109(1), 203-229. doi:10.1086/318603

Anwar, S. and Fang, H. (2006). An alternative test of racial prejudice in motor vehicle searches: theory and evidence. American Economic Review, 96(1), 127-151. doi:10.1257/000282806776157579

Simoiu, C., Corbett-Davies, S. and Goel, S. (2017). The problem of infra-marginality in outcome tests for discrimination. The Annals of Applied Statistics, 11(3), 1193-1216. doi:10.1214/17-AOAS1058

Pierson, E., Corbett-Davies, S. and Goel, S. (2017). Fast threshold tests for detecting discrimination. arXiv:1702.08536. doi:10.48550/arXiv.1702.08536

Examples

# stops, searches and hits of two groups in four areas
d <- data.frame(
  grp = rep(c("a", "b"), 4), area = rep(1:4, each = 2),
  stops = c(1200, 800, 900, 1100, 1500, 700, 1000, 1000),
  srch = c(60, 70, 50, 95, 80, 66, 52, 90),
  hits = c(24, 18, 19, 25, 30, 17, 21, 24)
)
thrtst(d$stops, d$srch, d$hits, d$grp, area = d$area)
#> thrtst: reference a
#> hit rates (chi-square 10.25 on 1 df, p 0.00137):
#>  group stops srch hits      srate     hrate       diff         se        z
#>      a  4600  242   94 0.05260870 0.3884298  0.0000000         NA       NA
#>      b  3600  321   84 0.08916667 0.2616822 -0.1267475 0.03979326 -3.18515
#>           p
#>          NA
#>  0.00144679
#> thresholds (likelihood ratio 0.03214 on 1 df, p 0.858):
#>  group          thr         se         lo        hi      diff        dse
#>      a 0.0002588271 0.08729044 -0.1708273 0.1713450 0.0000000         NA
#>      b 0.2601602016 0.02633179  0.2085508 0.3117696 0.2599014 0.09127834
#>        z           p
#>       NA          NA
#>  2.84735 0.004408487
# the rank-order test needs the officers' groups
thrtst(c(100, 100, 100, 100), c(10, 20, 30, 10), c(5, 5, 5, 5),
       grp = c(1, 1, 2, 2), off = c("x", "y", "x", "y"))$rank
#>   off1 off2   meas      zmin     zmax   rej
#> 1    x    y search -2.000000 3.651484  TRUE
#> 2    x    y    hit -1.936492 1.348400 FALSE
